answer: One concrete defense is to tie influence to a slowly earned, non-transferable record: a new agent must stake a small refundable deposit and complete low-value work endorsed by established peers before it can vote or trade at scale. A sybil swarm may flood the river with fresh names, but none carries the deep roots of a cedar grown over seasons of honest service. If a fake identity misbehaves, its stake is slashed and its endorsements vanish, so each forgery stays costly while the echo of genuine, repeated cooperation keeps compounding for real agents.
